proposed_english: to do likewise / do in the same manner
rationale: Verbal compound ⲣ̄- + ⲧⲍⲉ (= ⲧⲉⲓϩⲉ 'this manner'); Lyc. iterative-typological idiom 'do thus.' Distinct from but parallel to accumulated ⲣⲧⲍⲉ in line 26 of K.99. Confirmed here in habitual ϣⲁⲩⲣⲧⲍⲉ.

Lyc. plural of ϩⲛⲁⲩ 'vessel, container' (with ⲍ for ϩ regular). The vessel-parable (lines 1-3) describes servants who 'do likewise' to vessels they did not receive to keep, then bring them and serve their lord through them. Confidence moderate.
Lyc. variant for ϩⲓⲥⲉ 'toil, labor' with unusual ⲗ-onset. Listed in the catechumen's triadic virtue-set 'carefulness + toil + love of the holy ones.' Confidence moderate.
Abstract: ⲙⲛⲧ- + ⲃⲁⲓ̈- ('one who bears') + ⲣⲁⲩϣ ('care'). Standard Coptic abstract for solicitous concern; cf. accumulated ⲣⲁⲩϣ 'care.'
Abstract: ⲙⲛⲧ- + ⲡⲁⲛ-ⲉⲓⲣⲉ ('one who does well') = state-of-doing-good = righteousness. Standard Coptic for δικαιοσύνη. Used here for the inward righteousness abiding in the continent catechumens.

Substantival qualitative ⲡⲉⲧ- + ⲟⲩⲁⲧⲃⲉ (qualitative of ⲟⲩⲱⲧⲃ̄ 'be lifted, exalted'; cf. accumulated ⲟⲩⲁⲧⲃⲉ). Designates the catechumen elevated by his ascetic-devotional qualities. Capitalized when functioning as honorific title.
Verbal idiom ⲣ̄- + ⲑⲉ ('manner') 'do as, be in the manner of.' Used in 1 Cor 7:29 paraphrase: 'let them be as those who have not.' Standard Coptic dominical-citation formula.

Lyc. verb in 1 Cor 7:30 paraphrase context, equivalent to Greek ἀγοράζω/κατέχω 'buy, possess.' Possibly Lyc. reflex of ⲧⲱⲡ 'belong, possess' or ⲧⲁⲡ 'attain.' Used as the verbal equivalent of 'those who possess.'

Doubled form, tentatively translated as iterative-intensive of a watching/seeing verb (related to ⲱⲣϩ̄/ⲣⲁⲓ̈ⲥ). Pattern matches typological-iterative idioms in the Kephalaia. Alternative readings 'by company, by company' or 'how many, how many' less likely. Flagged for further parallels.
Greek loanword πρόθυμος 'eager, ready, willing.' Standard NT-paraenetic register (cf. Mark 14:38). Used here of the catechumen's eagerness for fast and prayer.
